HARBORTON, Meridia (AP) — A ferry carrying commuters across the Calder Strait lost power and drifted into a breakwater early Tuesday, killing four passengers and injuring thirty-one, the Meridian Maritime Authority said.

The authority released a preliminary incident summary, Report MM-2026-114, which found that the vessel's starboard generator failed nineteen minutes before the collision and that the backup system did not engage. Investigators have not determined why the backup failed.

"The crew followed the emergency procedure as written, and the procedure did not save the ship," said Ilse Vantorren, the authority's director of marine safety, at a briefing in Harborton. "We are treating the maintenance record as the center of this inquiry."

Coast guard commander Petar Rask told reporters that divers recovered the ferry's data recorder on Wednesday afternoon and handed it to the authority's technical team. According to Rask, the recorder covers the full forty minutes before the collision.

The operator, Calder Line Ferries, said in a statement that it had suspended service on the route and would cooperate with investigators. The company confirmed that the vessel passed an inspection in March and declined to answer questions about the generator's service history.

Port records reviewed by the authority show the ferry carried 212 passengers, below its licensed capacity of 340. Hospital officials in Harborton said nine of the injured remained in critical condition on Wednesday evening.

The transport ministry said it would publish the full findings within ninety days. Ministry spokesperson Dana Elverk said the review would also examine inspection intervals for the other six vessels in the operator's fleet.

A memorial service is planned for Friday at the Harborton waterfront, city officials said.
